chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from ʿAlī ibn Bilāl, who said:
I wrote to al-Ṭayyib al-ʿAskarī عليه السلام: Is it permissible that the fiṭrah on behalf of a man’s dependents—whether they are ten, fewer, or more—be given to one needy, like-minded man?
So he عليه السلام wrote: “Yes, do that.”

key_terms.افْعَلْ: do it; a direct authorization from the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.الْفِطْرَةُ: zakat al-fiṭrah, the obligatory charity given at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.عِيَالِ: dependents or household members supported by a person
key_terms.مُحْتَاجًا: a needy person in financial need
key_terms.مُوَافِقًا: one who is in agreement, i.e. a fitting or aligned recipient in context
key_terms.يَجُوزُ: is it permissible; indicates a legal ruling

ai.seo_question: Can zakat al-fiṭrah for an entire household be given to one needy person?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning zakat al-fiṭrah. It states that the fiṭrah due on behalf of a man's dependents may be given collectively to one needy and deserving recipient, even if the dependents are numerous.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.2071 - It is narrated by Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Bilal, who said:
"I wrote to Al-Tayyib Al-Askari (as), asking: 'Is it permissible to give the Zakat al-Fitr for a man's dependents, whether they are ten or fewer or more, to one needy and deserving person?'
Imam (as) wrote in reply: 'Yes, do that.'"
